Using the literature, group those positions into very specific genomic regions where many positions fall. Next, search for genes that are found in those genomic regions and that are more likely to cause the symptoms of Gulf War disease, putting an emphasis on metabolism, aging and altered physiology. The objective is to come up with a ranked list of genes (1 to 20) of greatest importance to the disease (finemapping) for each chromosome. Base the ranking on two main criteria: genomic distance to marker positions and functional relevance. A gene closer to any cluster should be given better ranking (closer to top), even better if its function is more relevant for the disease. In case of a tie between functional relevance and genomic distance, prioritize genomic distance.
